title: Creating and Managing Migrations
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of creating and managing migrations and at least two listed subtopics.
Interpret the creating and managing migrations example and predict its expected result.
Choose a verification step and identify one version, security, data, or troubleshooting consideration.

content.intro: Learn creating and managing migrations through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Creating and Managing Migrations matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: Visual guide: Creating and Managing Migrations
content_blocks.alt_text: Migration files represent schema changes; creating a migration and applying it are separate operations.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines creating and managing migrations as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: makemigrations; migrate; Understanding migration files; Reviewing generated operations; Applying migrations consistently. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

items.title: makemigrations
items.text: A migration is a versioned, ordered schema/data operation. `makemigrations` creates files; `migrate` applies them. Review generated operations and test the forward path and recovery plan using representative data.

items.title: migrate
items.text: For migrate, identify the Django component responsible, the inputs and outputs it owns, and the boundary conditions that matter. Use the accompanying example as a starting point, verify it with the official versioned documentation, and record one test demonstrating expected behavior.

items.title: Understanding migration files
items.text: Understanding migration files affects persistence and data correctness. Keep invariants in validation and database constraints where appropriate, inspect generated SQL/migrations, and test both expected data and error/rollback behavior.

items.title: Reviewing generated operations
items.text: Reviewing generated operations is part of the request/response contract. Match routes and methods explicitly, return an appropriate response/status, and test success, missing-resource and unauthorized paths.

items.title: Applying migrations consistently
items.text: A migration is a versioned, ordered schema/data operation. `makemigrations` creates files; `migrate` applies them. Review generated operations and test the forward path and recovery plan using representative data.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Creating and Managing Migrations
content_blocks.code:
python manage.py makemigrations catalog
python manage.py sqlmigrate catalog 0001
python manage.py migrate
content_blocks.expected_output: makemigrations creates a migration file; sqlmigrate shows SQL for a chosen migration; migrate applies pending migrations.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.
content_blocks.troubleshooting: Review migrations and back up important data before production schema changes. Migration names depend on your project.

content_blocks.title: Guided walkthrough
content_blocks.text: First identify the input and the responsible Django component. content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Change one input or configuration choice related to makemigrations. Write down the expected outcome, test one normal case and one invalid or boundary case, then record what changed. Do not add real credentials or sensitive production data.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.

content_blocks.title: Recap
content_blocks.text: You should now be able to describe creating and managing migrations, explain the listed topics, inspect the example, and choose an appropriate verification step. Keep the scope and version caveat visible when sharing your solution.
